composition_answer: YES. The committed single-use release at head cef478d6f8d78f0b13b236b7874e32d4b626ec0f is sufficient to execute exactly one checkpoint-free representative routed aggregate on the accepted F017 proof/reference surface, without re-executing experts and without authorizing any shared-expert, FFN-completion, residual, or S2 work. Every binding was independently recomputed from committed bytes: the release binds the accepted authorization d103ab6a..., arithmetic contract ef4b6f5c..., executor fa855586..., final cycle-02 review 3c362e0b... (ACCEPT, zero blocking and zero non-blocking-required findings), synthetic rehearsal 064d938d..., expert-output reuse authorization 1b8b053d..., private manifest 2b3a0ef3..., plus the newly load-bearing wrapper 6822eb18..., terminalizer 29169be6..., path contract f9f2e24f..., publication contract c85c40b6..., validator 725a4f23..., and release rehearsal 1b6b4476.... All load-bearing execution bytes (executor, wrapper, terminalizer, ledger adapter, all four contracts) are byte-identical between the bound execution code head d38a42ad... and the reviewed head; the only post-code-head code change is a strictly narrowing validator hardening that pins previously length-only SHA declarations. The exact eight ID-weight-output triples in canonical order [250,10,237,62,73,177,218,28] (with expert 62 before the heavier-weighted 73, excluding any weight sort) join byte-equal across release, authorization, reuse authorization (modulo semantic_role), and the COMPLETE expert execution evidence; real mode requires the eight exact protected SHAs so neither the historical direct-DPREFIX output nor any production serial-f32 artifact can leak in, and the production serial-f32 surface remains a declared separate unauthorized surface with serial-binary32, BLAS, parallel, and GPU reduction forbidden by the frozen arithmetic contract, which the executor implements literally: exact binary32-to-binary64 promotion, one binary64 product per term, one direct CPython 3.14.6 math.fsum call per coordinate over the ordered 8-tuple, little-endian f64[6144], 49152 bytes, environment mismatch failing before input consumption. Concrete path semantics are fixed and not caller-selectable: the wrapper hard-codes pathlib-home/repository expressions for retained inputs, state root, output root/file, approval, and GO token, pins the release to its committed repository path, and rejects a copied release; because the state root and output are $HOME-anchored, even a copied checkout converges on the same exclusive machine-local state. Preflight validates every locally checkable requirement before any aggregate computation: reconstructed ledger 175 (from the sha-pinned M1F0 execution result, receipts 167-175, COMPLETE), exact code and contract bytes, the subprocess repo-mode release validator, runtime environment, all eight retained inputs open-once with EXPECTED=BEFORE=CONSUMED=AFTER on manifest-verified read-only single-link descriptors, absent attempt state and absent authoritative output, fixed paths, output-parent open-once, storage, and same-filesystem; this review ran the wrapper production preflight and reproduced the preparation packet SHA dd39aaa2... exactly, with truthful zero counters. One-shot semantics are durable: authorization requires the future committed independent approval (exact key set, ACCEPT verdict, exact statement, release and authorization SHA bindings, code-head binding, approval_does_not_execute and approval_is_not_token both true) plus a GO token at the fixed path whose exact eight fields bind the approval SHA and release SHA; eighteen forged/mutated approval-and-token variants, the approval-as-token, the prepared-release-as-token, and a token bound to a different approval were all rejected in fresh attacks while the exact join is satisfiable. Consumption is an exclusive atomic mkdir plus fsynced durable attempt-start before aggregate computation; concurrent losers cannot start, duplicate attempts are rejected, and all interruption windows reconcile deterministically through the read-only terminalizer (no-durable-start blocks, output-without-attempt blocks, interrupted-no-output is consumed, published-output-without-terminal is recovered with authority, wrong terminal output identity blocks, hard-linked or symlinked outputs block). Publication is exclusive-temp, file fsync, chmod 0400, no-replace hard link relative to the validated 0700 directory descriptor, parent fsync, unlink, parent fsync, then read-back verification of exactly 49152 finite little-endian binary64 bytes; symlinked or preexisting destinations and writable-alias or symlinked directories are rejected, and a durable published output survives later evidence failure for reconciliation. No checkpoint, shard, expert, shared, FFN, residual, S2, GPU, BLAS, parallel, or alternate executor path exists in the bound code, and the executor's own --execute mode rejects the prepared release, the approval, and the GO token as its release argument. Zero additional real reproduction runs is correct under committed authority: the accepted authorization budgets exactly one real aggregate execution (future_aggregate_execution_count 1), a real reproduction would exceed that budget, and determinism is already frozen by the accepted two-fresh-process bit-identical synthetic rehearsal on the pinned environment together with read-back output verification and post-aggregate input re-verification on the same descriptors; both committed rehearsal evidence files regenerate byte-identically. Remaining findings are defense-in-depth only; the GO token, the committed independent approval, and ledger movement remain future separately authorized events outside this review.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: Executor --execute remains an alternate caller-path surface activatable only by forging an approval-status document
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: The bound executor's --execute mode accepts caller-selected --state-root/--output/--output-root and validates a ten-key release document with status INDEPENDENTLY_APPROVED that no committed or planned artifact matches: this review verified fresh-process that the committed prepared release and a well-formed GO token are both rejected at 'release schema keys', so activating this surface requires self-authoring a document asserting independent approval, which is willful forgery outside the mechanical enforcement model. Cycle-02 (RRA-C2-D1) prescribed closing the operational path by pinning paths or shipping an enforcing wrapper; the release delivers the enforcing wrapper with fixed non-caller-selectable paths, satisfying that prescription. Because the wrapper's state root and output are $HOME-anchored, any post-success willful re-invocation of the wrapper also collides with the consumed fixed state root.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: Release validator does not check output_publication.finite
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: Of 36 independent adversarial release-document mutations run by this review, exactly one survived: setting output_publication.finite to false still validates, because the validator checks dtype, shape, byte_length, serialization, fsync, no-replace, overwrite, and partial-authority fields but not the finite flag. Enforcement is redundant in code (executor requires finite inputs, products, and aggregate; wrapper read-back requires finite; terminalizer requires finite) and the committed release bytes declare finite true with the approval binding the exact release SHA, so no execution-time behavior depends on this validator field.
defense_in_depth_findings.required_fix: Optional hardening: add req(output.get("finite") is True, "output finiteness") to the release validator.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: Wrapper does not hash-pin the release validator bytes before executing it
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: Wrapper preflight subprocess-runs the on-disk validator, which in repo mode verifies all twelve release bindings including the wrapper and terminalizer bytes, but nothing at runtime verifies the validator's own bytes against the release binding 725a4f23... except the validator itself. The wrapper's independent critical gates (authorization/arithmetic/executor SHAs, fixed release path and identity, ledger, environment, fixed paths, absences, approval and token bindings) do not depend on the validator, and a tampered wrapper defeats any in-process check anyway, so the residual exposure is bounded to review-mechanics checks and closed procedurally by the approval binding the release SHA that pins the validator.
defense_in_depth_findings.required_fix: Optional hardening: in validate_fixed_bindings, require sha256 of the validator file to equal the release's release_validator binding before the subprocess call.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: Executor synthetic mode can pre-create a file at the fixed authoritative output path (denial only, no authority)
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: Synthetic rehearsal mode takes a caller-chosen --output and does not refuse the fixed authoritative output expression, so a willful pre-approval synthetic run could create routed-aggregate.f64le at the authoritative path, permanently fail-closing the real event (wrapper preflight rejects a preexisting output before attempt start). Such a file can never acquire authority: the terminalizer reports output-without-attempt as an accounting integrity blocker, authority requires the durable attempt-start plus terminal chain, and synthetic mode cannot consume or reproduce the protected representative bytes (declaration-time and consumed-bytes rejection verified in cycle-02 and re-verified by committed tests here). Extends carried RRA-C2-D3 (synthetic blocklist omits the historical direct-DPREFIX identity and manifest-root rejection), unchanged.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: Preflight does not assert pre-approval absence of the GO token and approval
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: The path contract requires the GO token and independent approval to not exist before independent approval, and the release prohibits a GO token in this phase, but wrapper --preflight-only only refuses a --go-token argument and does not check the fixed token path or approval path for premature existence. A premature token has no effect (execution additionally requires the committed approval with exact bindings), and this review verified on the review machine that the attempt state root, the GO token, the authoritative output, and the repository approval file are all currently absent.
defense_in_depth_findings.required_fix: Optional hardening: in preflight, require the fixed go_token path and approval path absent while release status is PREPARED_FOR_INDEPENDENT_APPROVAL.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: head_semantics append-only phrasing versus post-code-head validator modification
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: The release declares APPEND_ONLY_RELEASE_REVIEW_APPROVAL_AND_BANKING_COMMITS_PERMITTED after the execution code head d38a42ad..., but commit 38f617e modified the existing release validator file rather than only appending files. This review verified the modification is strictly narrowing (pins the execution code head and five previously length-only SHA declarations to exact constants) and that every load-bearing execution artifact (executor, wrapper, terminalizer, ledger adapter, authorization, arithmetic, path, and publication contracts) is byte-identical between d38a42ad... and the reviewed head; the release binds the hardened validator by exact SHA. Documentation-consistency note only.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: Carried cycle-02 residuals unchanged
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: Two accepted cycle-02 residuals carry unchanged: a concurrent race loser exits with an uncaught FileExistsError traceback instead of a FAIL_CLOSED packet (still fail-closed: the loser computes nothing and writes nothing, and the wrapper's begin_attempt likewise precedes any aggregate work), and st_nlink==1 plus read-only mode cannot exclude a pre-existing foreign write-open descriptor on retained inputs (fully mitigated because consumed bytes are the validated first-read bytes and the AFTER re-read on the same device/inode descriptor detects tampering).
